summary: Brad Gerstner is bullish on OpenAI, citing its $20B annualized run rate and continued momentum; he has bought more shares and believes both OpenAI and Anthropic should go public to access cheap capital and expand the retail investor base.

summary: Chamath is skeptical about the quality and durability of Anthropic's revenue, arguing much of it reflects experimental test budgets rather than mission-critical production workflows, and that the industry's breathless messaging is creating a dangerous PR backlash that threatens future data center buildout.
quote: There's not a single good example that we can find of sustained positive margin expansion and impact of AI inside of a true corporate enterprise that is not right now a small test.

summary: Jason frames the oil price volatility as significant but contextualizes it historically, noting Brent crude spiked from $84 to $119 and back, currently at $99, with the Strait of Hormuz closure adding major uncertainty to the duration and direction of price moves.
quote: Brent crude oil...it spiked to $84 on Friday....$119 on Monday...dropped back down to $84, jumped back up to $100 after 3 commercial ships were hit...Brent crude currently at $99 when we're taping this.

summary: Brad (Guest) acknowledges oil's short-term inflationary spike but believes the Trump doctrine limits conflict duration, implying oil price impacts will be shorter-lived than feared. He also notes Goldman Sachs raised PCE inflation forecasts largely due to oil.
quote: I think the Trump doctrine is far more pragmatic than the neocon doctrine...my suspicion is that these impacts are shorter duration, but right now the market's having a little bit of post-traumatic stress flashbacks to Afghanistan and Iraq.

summary: Chamath is bullish on oil prices coming back down, arguing Trump's 'war will be over soon' comments triggered a rapid drop from $120 to $90, validating market belief in a short conflict. He also highlights coordinated IEA strategic reserve releases (~400M+ barrels) as a further dampener on price spikes.
quote: President Trump was asked about the war and he said the war would be over very soon. What did the market do? The market literally took oil from $120 a barrel to $90 a barrel...Chris released 172 million barrels...a coordinated release of about 400 million barrels of petroleum. That's going to dampen the effect of any price spike.

summary: Sacks warns of severe upside oil price risk if escalation continues — Iranian tit-for-tat strikes on Gulf oil and gas infrastructure could devastate production across the region even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens, representing a worst-case bull scenario for oil prices.
quote: If the Iranians get hit, if their oil and gas infrastructure gets hit, they've already said they're going to engage in tit-for-tat retaliation against the Gulf states...it won't really matter if the straits get reopened because you won't be able to restart oil and gas production in the Middle East.
